newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia to simplify environmental laws.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia to simplify environmental laws.

text.p: Australia's federal government said on Tuesday it would simplify environmental laws, limiting itself to approving projects of national significance and handing other matters to the states.

A single set of regulations would remove the current duplication of assessments, a spokesman for Environment Minister Robert Hill told Reuters. Under the new system the federal government would consider environmental approval for projects of national significance involving international treaty obligations, cross state borders, national parks or endangered species, or involving nuclear matters, the spokesman said.
The federal government would also be able to examine projects involving big investment levels, he said, with the six state governments assessing less significant projects.
Hill said the national significance provisions would provide the trigger for federal government involvement.

"Under this new proposal which will replace existing triggers which are really somewhat irrelevant with a trigger of national environmental importance, then these matters will be looked at by the Commonwealth government as they should be," Hill told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.

"What the states are saying to us (the federal government) is that they can't see why we're involved in a whole lot of matters that are really of state significance and not of national significance and we agree," Hill said.
Hill would have to consult the states before the details of the plan could be completed by the end of 1997.
